articles.title: The Batman 2 is delayed to 2027, but Mickey 17’s release date is moving up
articles.summary: The Batman Part II has been delayed until October 1st 2027, Warner Bros. has announced. An unnamed film starring Tom Cruise will its place on October 2nd, 2026.
articles.body: If you’ve been waiting patiently to see how Matt Reeves’ story for The Batman continues once the reboot’s sequel arrives, you’ll have to wait a little longer. It was once set to open October 2nd, 2026, after an initial delay caused by the Hollywood writers’ strike derailed Warner Bros. plans to release it in 2025, but the studio has now announced that it’s pushing The Batman Part II even further back to October 1st, 2027, according to Variety. It appears the most recent shift could be strategic. Variety adds that Warner Bros. has rushed to fill that October 2nd, 2026, slot with an unnamed film featuring Tom Cruise and directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu. While that sucks for fans of the bat, one nice consolation is news that Bong Joon-Ho’s Mickey 17 is coming even sooner than expected; it is now scheduled for March 7th, 2025, after delays of its own caused the original 2024 release to slip. Mickey 17 stars Robert Pattinson (who also plays Bruce Wayne in The Batman Part II) and is directly inspired by the Edward Ashton novel Mickey7, which follows a willingly and literally disposable employee through his many doors of death. Also starring in the film are Steven Yeun, Naomi Ackie, Toni Collette, Mark Ruffalo, and Thomas Turgoose. Warner Bros. reportedly swapped its release date with Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, which now opens April 18th, to give Mickey 17 more time on Imax screens.

articles.title: Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3' makes Rs 273 crore, approximately $28.4 million in its opening weekend, beats Tom Cruise's 'Digger' which has made Rs $ 20 million
articles.summary: Indian films have occasionally made a strong impact at the global box office, but very few have managed to finish ahead of major Hollywood releases during
articles.body: Indian films have occasionally made a strong impact at the global box office, but very few have managed to finish ahead of major Hollywood releases during the same weekend. Films such as ‘RRR’, ‘Jawan’ and ‘Kalki 2898 AD’ have made their presence felt internationally, while ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’ also emerged as a major global success. However, Ajay Devgn-starrer ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ has now achieved a new milestone by finishing ahead of a Tom Cruise film in a direct box-office clash.The third instalment of the ‘Drishyam’ franchise has emerged as the second highest-grossing film worldwide over its opening weekend. The film had a powerful start in India, collecting Rs 62 crore net on its opening day. It maintained its momentum over the weekend and ended its first three days with Rs 176.50 crore net, translating to around Rs 211.80 crore or $22 million gross.The film also made its presence felt in overseas markets. While its opening in the US and Canada was not as explosive as its performance in India, it still managed to put up a respectable number. According to Comscore and Box Office Mojo, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ earned $2.7 million across North America from slightly more than 500 theatres.Its performance in other international territories has been stronger, with markets across Europe and the Gulf contributing more than $3.4 million. By Sunday, the film had accumulated an estimated $28.4 million, or approximately Rs 273 crore, worldwide.That figure placed ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ at No. 2 globally for the weekend. The only film ahead of it was Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson's erotic thriller ‘Verity’, which registered a massive $62.6 million worldwide, including $32 million from the US and Canada.More significantly, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ finished ahead of Tom Cruise's ‘Digger’, which also arrived in cinemas during the weekend. The film marked Cruise's return to director-backed projects after a series of action-heavy outings but opened to around $20 million worldwide, falling short of the Ajay Devgn-starrer.The Hindi film also finished ahead of another major Hollywood release, Brad Pitt's ‘Heart of the Beast’. The latter collected $28 million in its second weekend, placing it third globally. ‘Resident Evil’ rounded off the top five with an estimated weekend worldwide collection of $24.5 million.‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ brings back Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, alongside Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also returns from ‘Drishyam 2’ in a cameo, while Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj are the new additions to the cast.Written and directed by Abhishek Pathak, the film hit theatres on October 2, a significant date for the franchise. Unlike the first two Hindi films, which were remakes of the Malayalam ‘Drishyam’ films, the third instalment follows an original story and takes the franchise in a new direction.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Pedro Piqueras explica por qué la legislatura de Pedro Sánchez ha sido “atroz” y expone la razón principal del adelanto electoral: “Se ha quedado solo”
articles.standfirst: El colaborador de ‘Mañaneros 360’ responsabiliza a los partidos de derecha por los “insultos”
articles.summary: El colaborador de ‘Mañaneros 360’ responsabiliza a los partidos de derecha por los “insultos”
articles.body: Ya es una realidad. El próximo 29 de noviembre, España tendrá elecciones generales. Pedro Sánchez las ha convocado este mismo lunes 5 y, ahora, todos los partidos se preparan para meses de crispación, debate y programas políticos. En ‘Mañaneros 360’ han contado con Pedro Piqueras para hablar de la decisión del presidente del Gobierno y las razones del adelanto electoral. A su juicio, era algo necesario porque era “una legislatura que ya no tiene mucho sentido seguir”. Sobre los motivos que han terminado provocando que las elecciones generales se adelanten un año, tampoco tiene dudas: “Le han fallado los apoyos en un momento crucial, como era el de la vivienda”. Pedro Piqueras detalla que, a su modo de ver, nunca se pudo considerar a Junts un aliado fiel para el actual Gobierno: “Ha sido ventajista en el sentido de conseguir acuerdos relacionados con la amnistía y otros asuntos para Cataluña, pero, en los momentos decisivos, ha negociado muy fuerte”. También ha querido responsabilizar a los partidos de derecha por la “polarización” actual que vive la sociedad española: “Creo que para el presidente del Gobierno ha sido una legislatura atroz, han sido tres años de polarización. Es más culpa de la derecha, por los insultos que se lanzaban contra Pedro Sánchez, las polémicas parlamentarias, a veces de una dureza…”. Asimismo, reconoce que se han dicho cosas en los mitines o en el Congreso de los Diputados que a él mismo le ruborizaría decir en televisión. “Era una legislatura que tenía que terminar cuanto antes. El presidente del Gobierno se ha quedado un poco solo y yo creo que, desde mi punto de vista, no tenía más remedio”, zanja Piqueras en RTVE sobre este asunto.

articles.title: In 2023, Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos teamed up to protect the Amazon rainforest; $200 million commitment brought their nonprofits together
articles.summary: In 2023, Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos announced a $200 million partnership to protect the Amazon rainforest through their nonprofit organizations. The initiative aims for zero deforestation and the protection of biodiversity.
articles.body: Back in 2023, ‘One Battle After Another’ star Leonardo DiCaprio paired up with American businessman Jeff Bezos, who is also known as the second-richest person on Earth. The two unlikely forces came together to fight for the Amazon rainforest, which has been depleting in size and quality for a variety of reasons.When Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos worked together on raising funds for the Amazon rainforestIn July 2023, as per reports shared online by the Associated Press, DiCaprio and Bezos' nonprofit organizations collaborated to launch a dedicated fund for the Amazon rainforest, along with Vice President Lauren Sánchez. They committed over USD 200 million through the Protect Our Planet (POP) Challenge for the cause.The pledge focused on supporting Brazil's environmental goals, which included achieving zero deforestation in the Amazon and safeguarding protected areas and Indigenous areas as well. The funds were meant to be invested in things like municipal and national programs that may help achieve zero illegal deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon. Not only that, but the funding was also established to reinforce and help with physical monitoring, infrastructure, and ecological management of existing national parks.At the time, DiCaprio shared a statement about the collaboration between him and Bezos, saying, “We are inspired by Brazil’s ambitious goals for protecting the Amazon, one of the most important places for wildlife on the planet, and are thrilled to be able to support these efforts through the Protecting Our Planet Challenge.”One of the representatives of Bezos’ nonprofit, Cristián Samper, also explained at the time that “Amazon is critical for the future of global biodiversity and climate, and we welcome the commitment from President Lula and the Government of Brazil to protect it. We are pleased to support the designation and management of protected areas and Indigenous territories as a key part of the strategy to reduce deforestation, along with new economic models of development based on the conservation and sustainable use of the forest.”Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos extended the project and launched the Phoenix Species ProjectThey invested additional money into the project to start a brand new branch that mainly focused on preventing the extinction of 100 of the world's most critically endangered species. Some of the priority species that were named in the program included the golden-crowned sifaka (Madagascar lemur), Malayan pangolins, and the pink land iguana in the Galápagos.The main objective of the program was to move away from short-term goals and instead invest their funding into sustained multi-year habitat protection and species breeding/restoration programs to ensure that these species do not cease to exist.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ star Isaiah Washington reveals his wife died more than a year ago
articles.summary: Former “Grey’s Anatomy” star Isaiah Washington revealed in an Instagram post that his wife of 29 years, Jenisa Washington — who also went by Jenisa Garland — died more than a year ago.
articles.body: Former “Grey’s Anatomy” star Isaiah Washington revealed in an Instagram post over the weekend that his wife of 29 years, Jenisa Washington, died more than a year ago. Appearing to address speculation, Washington said that “the rumors are true” and that his wife — who also went by Jenisa Garland — had “collapsed suddenly” in May 2025 and died on June 9, 2025. “It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family. She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered,” he wrote Saturday. “Listen, y’all…some headaches are not just headaches or migraines, they can be much worse and a warning sign. Get a brain scan if you can and take those headaches seriously.” A hemorrhagic stroke occurs when a blood vessel in the brain bursts, causing bleeding in or around the brain, according to the National Library of Medicine’s MedlinePlus. The bleeding increases pressure inside the skull and damages brain tissue. Common causes include an aneurysm, high blood pressure, head trauma or arteriovenous malformation. According to MedlinePlus, symptoms can include a sudden severe headache, sudden dizziness or trouble walking, sudden confusion, and sudden numbness or weakness in the face. “She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy,” the actor said. Washington didn’t say why he waited over a year to announce her death but suggested that she may not have wanted the information made public. “I don’t know if this is an appropriate post, because Jenisa Washington was extremely private, but I guess I just have to be reprimanded from her on the other side,” he wrote. Celebrities including Viola Davis, Loni Love, Michael Beach, Tichina Arnold and Neil Brown Jr. offered their condolences to Washington. Washington appeared on “Grey’s Anatomy” as Dr. Preston Burke but was fired in 2007 after he used a homophobic slur against a co-star. He later apologized.

articles.title: In 2015, Josh Hartnett sold his US homes; years later, the Verity star made a Hampshire farm his permanent home with wife Tamsin Egerton and 4 kids
articles.summary: Josh Hartnett may have spent the early part of his career as one of Hollywood’s most recognisable leading men, but his life away from the cameras looks
articles.body: Josh Hartnett may have spent the early part of his career as one of Hollywood’s most recognisable leading men, but his life away from the cameras looks remarkably different. The actor, known for films including Pearl Harbor, Black Hawk Down and Oppenheimer, now lives with his wife, British actress Tamsin Egerton, and their four children in the Hampshire countryside in England.At the centre of Hartnett’s quieter life is the family’s small farm. Rather than a sprawling celebrity estate, he has described it as a “tiny little farm”, where everyday family life unfolds alongside a collection of animals. In a recent appearance on the UK show This Morning, Hartnett gave a glimpse into just how busy the household can get. “We’ve got a little farm, tiny little farm,” Hartnett said. “A lot of animals, we have four kids, so it’s busy. “My life is my family life, and then every once in a while I come out and do something like this, which is such an anomaly for me.”A farm filled with animalsHartnett’s Hampshire home is not just about having a quieter address. The actor has previously spoken about the animals that are part of the family’s everyday routine.A report described mornings at the property as involving his four children as well as a dog, several guinea pigs, chickens and a small group of pygmy goats. Hartnett has a particular fondness for the goats and described them as exceptionally affectionate.The actor has also spoken about the simple pleasures of rural life, including feeding the goats and spending time outdoors with his children. The family’s move to the English countryside has allowed him to build a routine that is considerably removed from the intensity of his earlier Hollywood years.His life revolves around his familyHartnett and Egerton have four children, although the couple have deliberately kept their children’s names and most personal details away from the public eye. Their first three children were born in 2015, 2017 and 2019, while Hartnett confirmed in 2024 that they had welcomed a fourth child.The actor has repeatedly made it clear that being present for his family is a priority. In his recent interviews, he has spoken about how his family has helped him feel more grounded and comfortable with the attention that comes with his profession.His wife, Tamsin Egerton, has also largely stayed away from the spotlight despite having her own acting career. The couple have been together for years and quietly married in 2021.Why Josh Hartnett left Los AngelesHartnett’s decision to settle in England was not simply a change of scenery. At the height of his fame, he deliberately stepped back from the Hollywood machine because he did not want his career to become his entire identity. In a 2024 interview with The Guardian, he explained, “Hollywood is more than a place, it’s like a state of mind.”He continued, “If you’re around people who are constantly talking about the movie business, your life is going to be pretty much one note. And I’ve never wanted that.”Hartnett also had little affection for the practical realities of living in Los Angeles, adding, “I just never really vibed with L.A. because I’m not a big fan of sitting in the car all day.”The actor had reached a point where he was being offered major blockbuster roles, including Superman, but chose not to follow the conventional path to franchise stardom. He later explained that he did not want his life to be consumed by his profession.From Hollywood heart-throb to countryside lifeHartnett became a major star following films such as Pearl Harbor and Black Hawk Down, but instead of continually chasing bigger projects, he gradually chose a more private life and more selective work.His retreat from Hollywood did not mean he stopped acting. In recent years, he has appeared in projects including Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer, the Netflix series Black Mirror and M. Night Shyamalan’s Trap. He also appeared in The Bear and is currently promoting the thriller Verity.His approach to work has changed, however. The actor has spoken about choosing projects that interest him while keeping his family life at the centre of his priorities.For Hartnett, the contrast between his public career and private home could hardly be greater. One side involves film sets, premieres and press tours; the other involves four children, chickens, guinea pigs, a dog and his beloved pygmy goats on a small farm in the English countryside.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ms Rachel rips celebrities who do 'nothing during a genocide'
articles.summary: Ms. Rachel's Instagram post takes aim at celebrities she says are "doing nothing" amid the Gaza conflict
articles.body: Children's YouTube entertainer Ms. Rachel took another swipe at high-profile celebrities who have remained silent on Gaza in a social media post on Sunday, saying she is unimpressed by fame when public figures are "doing nothing" during what she has repeatedly called a genocide. "Do you want to meet insert huge celeb? Me: No," Rachel Griffin Accurso, known as Ms. Rachel, said in an Instagram post. "I don’t fan girl over someone who is doing nothing during a genocide." MOMS FOR LIBERTY CO-FOUNDER WARNS PARENTS ABOUT MS RACHEL’S POLITICAL ACTIVISM, ‘NOT MR ROGERS’ The post came less than a week after Campaign Against Antisemitism criticized Accurso in a statement to Fox News Digital over her declaration that she would not work with "privileged" people who stay silent about Gaza. A spokesperson from Campaign Against Antisemitism said that her standard amounted to an exclusionary political test. "Ms. Rachel’s comments on who she is willing to work with are patently hypocritical," the spokesperson said. "Acting as an adjudicator is a privileged position in and of itself, and subjecting people to political purity tests is by definition exclusionary. One would have thought that someone who has admitted to having – apparently accidentally – liked a comment online saying 'Free America from the Jews', Ms. Rachel would be taking care to avoid these sorts of topics entirely." "Evidently the temptation to ostracize those with differing views on the war in Gaza, many of whom will be Jews, is too strong for her to resist," they continued. MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT Accurso's expanding political profile had also drawn pushback from parents. Washington Examiner contributor, author and homeschooling mother Bethany Mandel accused Accurso of amplifying what she called a Hamas narrative, telling Fox News Digital last week that the children's entertainer had become an influential messenger about the war. "She is serving as their mouthpiece for a lot of Americans, not just children and not just the adults that follow her," Mandel said. Accurso did not identify the "huge celeb" she may have been referencing in her post. In the caption, however, she said she would still speak directly with prominent people if she believed she could persuade them to use their platforms. "I'd have a conversation with someone with a massive platform any day to try and convince them to speak out. (And I have)," Accurso said. MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV The post was the latest in a series of challenges Accurso has issued to celebrities concerning Gaza. Last month, she pledged to match rapper Macklemore's $1 million donation to Palestinian aid organizations and called on "every wealthy White celebrity" to do the same. During a separate appearance on comedian Ilana Glazer's "It's Open" podcast, she targeted celebrities she described as too famous to be canceled. Accurso questioned why celebrities with secure careers would not publicly advocate for civilians in Gaza during the podcast appearance. "If you are so famous, and you’re uncancellable, and you’re so famous and you won’t even say like, 'Kids in Gaza should have schools, people in Gaza should have hospitals.' Like you won't say something so basic and like why can't you risk something to help save lives?" Accurso said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The continued political activism comes as Accurso's media empire continues to grow. Accurso has more than 21 million YouTube subscribers and has donated roughly $22,500 to Democratic and progressive candidates since 2024. Her brand has also secured partnerships with Netflix, Penguin Random House and Spin Master.

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo threatens to 'hulk out' at Trump, GOP over voting rights at NYC event
articles.summary: Mark Ruffalo threatened to "hulk out" at a NYC rally targeting Trump and the Republican Party, urging Democrats to fight back in midterm elections.
articles.body: Actor Mark Ruffalo threatened to "hulk out" at a New York City event on Sunday in an expletive-filled rant targeting President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, who, he argued, were trying to stop Democrats "from taking our country back." During a "Hands Off Our Vote" event, Ruffalo sounded the alarm and said Republicans were trying to "steal" the midterm elections, according to Variety. "We got to get this dumba---, fool a--, tired a--, lame a--, duck a-- out of office. We got to make him a lame duck! We have to stop his policies now. Another two years of this, and who knows what he’ll be doing? He’s calling to throw Democrats out of the country," Ruffalo said, according to the outlet. "And he means it! The guy means everything he says. I know we’re all tired, we are so tired, but we can’t give up now ... They’re going to try and stop us from taking our country back, and we’re not going to let ’em. Trump, we’re not letting you! Hands off our f---ing vote!" Ruffalo said. MARK RUFFALO FIRES BACK AT PARAMOUNT OVER 'APPALLING' ANTISEMITISM ACCUSATION TIED TO ELLISON MERGER CRITICISM "I’m going to hulk out. You won’t like me when I’m angry," he said, after a member of the audience cheered him on, referencing his portrayal of Marvel Cinematic Universe's "The Incredible Hulk," Variety reported. "Hey, I’m still here! They thought I was out for the count — I’m still here, I’m still playing the Hulk," Ruffalo said. "We can’t hide. We have to be together, and we have to fight for each other and we have to be brave. Our time to be brave is coming, I’m telling you brothers and sisters," Ruffalo said, according to the outlet. "They’re going to do everything they can to keep us in our homes. They’re going to do everything they can to make us feel small. They’re going to do everything they can to make us feel lost, to make it feel inevitable. It’s not inevitable! We’re inevitable — the truth is inevitable," he said. CLINTON-APPOINTED JUDGE TRIGGERS APPEAL AFTER BLOCKING KEY VOTER CITIZENSHIP LAW The RNC fired back at Ruffalo in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Mark Ruffalo is clearly stuck in La La Land. In the real world, voter ID and proof of citizenship are wildly popular, and noncitizens keep turning up on voter rolls," Ally Triolo, the RNC's election integrity communications director, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Democrats fight commonsense safeguards because they believe they can't win when Republicans make it easier to vote and harder to cheat," Triolo said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The White House also shredded Ruffalo for his comments, saying the actor had "Trump Derangement Syndrome." "Mark Ruffalo is a no-talent loser who has totally beclowned himself by spewing disgusting lies and spreading hate due to his severe and incurable case of Trump Derangement Syndrome. He is so devoid of actual talent that nobody with any commonsense would ever watch him unless it was to laugh at his miserable failures," White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital. Ruffalo blasted the outcome of the long-running fight over Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery last week after a federal judge cleared the Hollywood megadeal to move forward Wednesday. Ruffalo, who had been one of the most vocal Hollywood opponents of the merger, called the outcome "incredibly disappointing." "This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs – it is a bad deal for this country and should never have been approved," Ruffalo wrote in a post on X.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This is an incredibly disappointing outcome for the hundreds of thousands of us who stood up to block it, but it's also not the end," he continued. "This grassroots movement isn't going to fade away and neither is our resolve. This was never about just one merger: this was about fighting back against corrupt oligarch billionaires trampling the interests of everyday people to line their own pockets." Fox News Digital reached out to Marvel Universe for comment.

articles.title: Sonu Nigam's new property deal: Singer buys three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for Rs 17 crore - Report
articles.summary: Sonu Nigam has bought three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for a combined Rs 17 crore.
articles.body: Sonu Nigam has bought three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for a combined Rs 17 crore. The deals were registered on August 6, 2026, and the details come from property registration documents.Details of Sonu Nigam's Andheri West purchaseAccording to the documents obtained by CRE Matrix, the units are in the Aston building in the Sundervan Complex on Lokhandwala Road. Two of them are adjoining commercial units on the first floor, while the third is an office on the ground floor.As per the documents, Sonu bought the two first-floor units from Singular Health Private Limited for Rs 16 crore. Together, they have a carpet area of 3,885.77 sq ft. The deal carried a stamp duty of Rs 96 lakh and also included four car parking spaces in the stack parking system in the building's basement.In a separate deal registered the same day, he bought the ground-floor office from the same seller for Rs 1 crore. It has a carpet area of 258.33 sq ft, and the stamp duty paid was Rs 6 lakh.Taken together, the three units have a carpet area of 4,144.10 sq ft, and the total value comes to Rs 17 crore. This works out to roughly Rs 41,021 per sq ft of carpet area. Sonu Nigam and Singular Health Private Limited could not be reached for a comment.Sonu Nigam's other real estate dealsThe singer has been in the news for several property deals over the last two years, including office spaces and land.In May 2026, he sold 1.067 hectares of land in Karjat, part of Mumbai 3.0, for Rs 95 lakh. In April 2026, he sold multiple land parcels totalling over 1.9 hectares in Karjat, a hill station in Raigad district near Mumbai, for Rs 1.95 crore. Both details are based on documents seen by CRE Matrix.In February 2026, his father, Agam Kumar Nigam, bought a 1,197 sq m land parcel in Mumbai's Madh Island for Rs 10 crore. The plot comes with a ground-plus-one-floor residential and commercial structure, according to documents seen by Liases Foras.In 2025, Sonu leased a commercial property in Santacruz East for five years at a total rent of over Rs 12.61 crore. The 4,257 sq ft office is in a building named Trade Centre BKC. It was leased to Pattni Hospitality, which runs a cafe and bar brand called Downtown 29. The deal was registered on December 2, 2025, as per documents reviewed by SquareYards.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Angelina Jolie: ‘I’ve learned to let go and move more quickly into the next place,’ a powerful life lesson on why leaving the past behind can help you move forward
articles.summary: Angelina Jolie has spoken out about the importance of moving on in life.
articles.body: Angelina Jolie has spoken out about the importance of moving on in life. Her journey from Hollywood stardom to humanitarian work has also seen her navigate several personal and professional chapters. Speaking in 2003 to Cosmopolitan, the actress spoke about putting the past behind and finding clarity in who a person truly is. And, as we look at today's quote of the day, we find another great reminder that life can drag us down if we do not learn to let go.Today's Motivational Quote of the Day, "It's hard to be clear about who you are when you are carrying around a bunch of baggage from the past. I've learned to let go and move more quickly into the next place."What does Angelina Jolie's quote mean?Jolie's quote is a commentary on the need to move on with life after events that affect a person. It speaks on how life can continue to drag a person down if they do not find a way to move on from what occurred. The quote is a reminder that life is not defined by the events that occur but how a person reacts to them and moves on in life.The quote is important todaybecause we often find ourselves stuck in the past with relationships, professional failures, personal failures, and life choices. The ability to move on is one of the most difficult aspects of growing older. With the constant ability to connect with people who have moved on with their lives, social media only adds to the challenge of putting the past behind us.Jolie's quote serves as a constant reminder that the past may affect who we are but should not define who we are destined to become. Letting go is the only way forward if we are to embrace the new and move on to the next level in life.Angelina Jolie's early lifeJolie was born on June 4, 1975, in Los Angeles, California, to a famous actor named Jon Voight and a model named Marcheline Bertrand. She was raised in the entertainment industry because she was born into a family of artists.Angelina Jolie's rise to fameJolie began to gain fame and critical acclaim for a string of successful film and television roles in the 1990s. For her role in the 1998 television film Gia , she received a Golden Globe.In 1999, with the film Girl, Interrupted , she received an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, which made her one of Hollywood's brightest rising stars. With films like Lara Croft: Tomb Raider, Mr. & Mrs. Smith, Wanted , and Salt , Angelina Jolie became an international movie star who was critically acclaimed. In addition to being an actress, she pursued a career in filmmaking and is well-known for humanitarian efforts, especially in relation to the refugee crisis.Her journey through various phases of life is a hallmark of a woman who has had to change and grow with every new chapter. Jolie's own words on the importance of moving on from the past are an appropriate reminder that growing older necessitates changes and that we need to put the past behind us to continue to move on in life.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Alba Carrillo, tajante: "Es incoherente ser de la clase obrera, ser mujer y votar a VOX"
articles.standfirst: La televisiva cree que es “ir en contra de los propios intereses”
articles.summary: La televisiva cree que es “ir en contra de los propios intereses”
articles.body: Este lunes, 5 de octubre, Pedro Sánchez compareció a primera hora de la mañana desde La Moncloa para comunicar que adelanta las elecciones generales al próximo domingo, 29 de noviembre. Todo ello, tras el periodo “de reflexión” que se había tomado este pasado fin de semana para meditar la decisión. El origen de esta decisión llegó tras tumbar el Congreso el pasado viernes los dos decretos en materia de vivienda en relación a la situación del desahucio de Maricarmen. Pues bien, las reacciones a este adelanto electoral no cesan en las últimas horas. El asunto se ha tratado en la entrega de ‘El Sótano’, programa que comanda Alba Carrillo en TEN TV. A él, invitaron a Estrella Galán, eurodiputada de Sumar, con quien abordaron el asunto al detalle. Pero más allá de esto, la reflexión de la presentadora sobre las próximas elecciones fue de lo más destacado. En primera instancia, Carrillo antes de comenzar a hablar con Galán comentó que iba a darle “una exclusiva”: “Una cosa que nunca he dicho. Me acusan mucho de ser sanchista, pero en las anteriores elecciones os voté a vosotras (Sumar). A veces, el PSOE me parece muy de derechas”, causando la impresión de la invitada. Tras ello, Galán reflexionó al respecto: “Vox ha colado el mensaje de odio a muchas personas que son de la clase trabajadora en Carabanchel, Vallecas o Villaverde. Estos votantes de la ultraderecha pueden ser desahuciados igualmente”. A estas palabras reaccionó Carrillo para sentenciar el asunto: “Perdón, pero eso es mío. Lleva mi nombre, el de Alba Carrillo. Es incoherente ser de la clase obrera, vivir en Vallecas y votar a VOX. Es ir en contra de tus propios intereses, es como ser mujer y votar a VOX, no puede ser”.

articles.title: Jeffrey Archer: Best-selling author and former politician dies aged 86
articles.summary: His last book, Adam and Eve, is set to release this month.
articles.body:
Bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86.

Archer sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and often set the novels in his home town of Wellington, Somerset.

In a statement, Archer's publisher HarperCollins said the author died "suddenly and peacefully at home" on Monday between writing sessions.

The former Conservative MP was jailed for perjury in 2001 after being found guilty of lying and cheating in his 1987 libel case against the Daily Star.

Jeffrey Archer obituary: successful novelist, disgraced politician and convicted liar

Archer was born in north London on 15 April 1940 but would quickly move to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where his family bought a house from John Cleese's mother.

In 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth.

He served as an MP for five years before becoming Conservative Party deputy chairman.

His political career was paused in 2001 when he was jailed for four years for perjury and perverting the course of justice.

He was found to have lied in libel action he had brought against The Star newspaper, in which he was awarded £500,000 in damages.

He was released in 2003 and returned to the House of Lords until he retired in 2024.

His last book, Adam and Eve, is set to be released this week, HarperCollins added, describing him as a "master storyteller" whose readers "meant everything to him".

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said at Wellington School.

Archer was due to attend the Cheltenham Festival on Saturday to discuss final his novel.

He and his wife Mary had celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary this year, HarperCollins said.

The pair have two sons and five grandchildren.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described Archer's death as a "huge shock".

Writing on X, she said: "I am incredibly saddened to hear this news. He had sent me a lovely message just this morning and was always a great source of encouragement to me personally."

Paying tribute to the bestselling author, Kate Elton, HarperCollins UK CEO and Jeffrey's editor, said: "It has been one of the great privileges of my publishing life to have been Jeffrey Archer's editor.

"He was the master storyteller and an editor's dream - phenomenally hard-working, utterly committed to completing draft after draft to get every word as perfect as possible, and a true champion of the 'team' nature of great publishing."

HarperCollins said the author had been at the Leicester Square Theatre in London on Sunday, signing books for fans with broadcaster Gyles Brandreth.

Writing on X, Brandreth said: "Just yesterday I did a show with Jeffrey Archer to celebrate his new novel – he said it was to be his last.

"He was in the most wonderful, ebullient form and had such a great reception from a packed house. He was funny, engaging and self-deprecating – a great storyteller to the last."

Former Conservative chancellor Nadhim Zahawi paid tribute to the bestselling author on X, describing him as a "dear friend and extraordinary human being".

He wrote: "His gift for storytelling was matched by his wit, warmth and boundless energy. Life was never dull in Jeffrey's company."

images.caption: Jeffrey Archer, pictured here with Margaret Thatcher, served as a Conservative MP and party chairman

articles.title: The Blue Planet and Gandhi composer George Fenton dies aged 76
articles.summary: The musician received five Oscar nominations, and soundtracked dozens of memorable nature films.
articles.body:
Composer George Fenton, whose work included music for films such as Gandhi, Groundhog Day and The Fisher King, as well as TV shows like Planet Earth and Bergerac, has died at the age of 76.

The prolific musician received five Oscar nominations for his film scores, including those for The Remains of the Day and Cry Freedom.

His work on the BBC TV show Blue Planet also earned awards from the Baftas, Emmy Awards and Ivor Novellos; and he also composed theme music for BBC News programmes such as Newsnight and Breakfast Time.

In a statement, Fenton's family said: "We are very sad to announce that George Fenton passed away unexpectedly today."

They continued: "He is survived by his loving wife Amanda, ex-wife Jane, children Gemma, Grace and Bridget, and grandchildren Lola, Audrey, Alfred, George, Frank and Beatrice, and a life of music."

Fenton was born George Howe in Bromley, Kent in 1949. According to a biography on his official website, his father was a mechanical engineer, and his mother had been a dancer before becoming a nurse during the war.

Both parents were musical - his father played drums and his mother played piano - but Fenton chose the electric guitar as his instrument at the age of seven.

That was "when music became more important than football," he later told The Express newspaper. "The Beatles had a huge influence on me."

He took his first lessons from a musician called Brian Rudd.

"He came into our lives as a chimney sweep, which he clearly wasn't," Fenton later recalled.

"My mother went mad at him because he filled the house with soot.

"As he left he said, 'I'm really sorry – but I tuned the boy's guitar for you.' She suggested that as compensation for the mess he could give me a lesson, which he did and then carried on doing."

Later, Fenton began to study the church organ, but rejected the chance to attend university and music college to pursue a career as a performer.

In 1968, he appeared in Alan Bennett's first West End play Forty Years On and was forced to adopt his mother's maiden name, as union rules prevented two actors from having the same name.

During that production, he also understudied the musical director of the show, Carl Davis - who similarly became a prominent composer for film and television.

A year later, he signed a record deal, and scored a top 10 hit in Sweden with a cover of The Beatles' Maxwell's Silver Hammer, but his career as a solo artist was short lived.

In the mid-1970s, he had a recurring role as soldier Martin Gimbel in the ITV soap opera Emmerdale Farm.

But as time went on, he found that directors were always casting him in roles that required him to play an instrument, so he decided to make music his main focus.

Fenton got his first job as composer and musical director for a production of Twelfth Night at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1974.

Eight years later, he was nominated for an Oscar for his score for Richard Attenborough's Gandhi, on which he worked with Indian composer and instrumentalist Ravi Shankar to develop a score reflecting the country's musical traditions.

It was only his fourth attempt at film music, and he was still almost entirely self-taught.

Throughout the 1980s, he wrote the soundtrack for a number of TV series, including the Bafta-winning The Jewel in the Crown, The Monocled Mutineer, and Alan Bennett's Talking Heads.

He also wrote many well-known theme tunes, including the BBC's One O'Clock News, Six O'Clock News, Nine O'Clock News, Newsnight, The Money Programme, and Radio 4's PM Programme.

For 1987's Cry Freedom - the story of South African campaigner Steve Biko, who was brutally killed by police - he worked with South African jazz musician Jonas Gwangwa, earning two Oscar nominations for best original score and song.

Almost by accident, the title track featured Fenton singing a list of anti-apartheid activists imprisoned or killed by the South African government.

He'd initially recorded the lyrics as a guide for Gwangwa - but the musician decided to keep some of them intact "as a gesture of brotherhood".

"Then it got nominated for an Oscar, so I then found myself singing it on live television to about a billion people, which was not what I intended at all," Fenton later told Radio 4's Desert Island Discs.

After composing the score for the BBC's Trials of Life in 1990, Fenton went on to create the music for what became known as David Attenborough's Earth Trilogy: The Blue Planet, Planet Earth and Frozen Planet.

Fenton's music perfectly complemented the stunning visuals of the ocean's depths and the polar ice caps, adding an emotional weight to the narrative, using the full might of the orchestra to evoke everything from wonder and awe to tension and suspense.

Following the success of the documentaries, Fenton created a show - The Blue Planet in Concert - which has been performed by leading orchestras in venues around the world.

Among his other well-known soundtracks were The Long Walk Home, You've Got Mail, Sweet Home Alabama, The Lady In The Van and Mrs Henderson Presents.

Fenton also scored more films for British director Ken Loach than any other composer.

Their 18 collaborations included Ladybird, Ladybird; I, Daniel Blake and The Wind That Shakes the Barley, which won the Palme d'Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival.

He also founded the Association of Professional Composers, which later merged with The Ivors Academy; and he is one of only a handful of musicians to receive the Academy's fellowship, alongside Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber, Sir Elton John, Kate Bush, Bruce Springsteen and George Michael.

In addition, Fenton was a visiting professor at the Royal College of Music and the University of Nottingham. He was made a CBE for services to music in 2023.

The composer often said that his musical career had been an accident, but nothing gave him greater joy than seeing his work come to life.

On his episode of Desert Island Discs, Fenton chose one of his own compositions - Reunion, from the soundtrack to the movie Accidental Hero - as it reminded him of watching pianist John Lowe play the melody in the studio.

"If I was sitting on a desert island and thinking about what a good time I'd had writing music, which I have, I want just one thing to remind me about the best part - which is the fact that you write something and then you're so surprised and thrilled at the way it's played," he told Sue Lawley.

"For a composer, that's the biggest kick you can get."

images.caption: George Fenton was one of the UK's most prolific and successful composers

"Yes … the rumors are true," Washington wrote on social media. "My dear wife of 29 years collapsed suddenly on May 31, 2025 and passed away on June 9, 2025. SANDRA BULLOCK SAYS BRYAN RANDALL WAS ILL FOR 'HALF OF OUR RELATIONSHIP' AS SHE OPENS UP ABOUT HIS DEATH "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered." articles.title: We shot the last film to be made in 'Scotland's Chernobyl'
articles.summary: Sci-fi horror comedy, Behind, features scenes filmed in Port Glasgow's Clune Park shortly before it was demolished.
articles.body:
A short film has captured some of the last images of a derelict housing estate nicknamed "Scotland's Chernobyl" before demolition crews moved in.

The tenements at Clune Park in Port Glasgow were built a century ago as housing for shipyard workers but most of the buildings lay empty for years.

Glasgow-based filmmaker Alessio Avezzano shot scenes for his post-apocalyptic sci-fi horror comedy, Behind, on the estate before bulldozers moved in last May.

"It's the last film to be made there. It was announced it would be demolished the day we were filming - we managed to get in there not a moment too soon," said the Scottish-Italian writer and director.

Redevelopment of Clune Park had been delayed for years due to a stand-off between private landlords and the local council, leaving the site frozen in time with just a handful of tenants remaining.

Large parts of the site became run-down and comparisons were made with the Ukrainian city of Pripyat, abandoned after the 1986 explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear plant led to a huge radiation leak.

The plot for Behind was inspired by "butt dialling", accidentally calling someone from a phone placed in a back pocket.

In the film, it has devastating consequences.

Avezzano said he come up with the idea while trying to write a script.

"That week my cousin, who hadn't done this before or since, just started to butt dial me every day and by the fifth day the light bulb moment came," he said.

"It is basically taking the idea of butt dials and what if they were a symptom of something more deadly."

Avezzano added: "It's got elements of how we responded to the pandemic and it's got elements of phone addiction and social media addiction."

Avezzano said Clune Park gave him the ideal backdrop for the short, and scenes were shot in areas accessible to the public.

Scenes for 2013's sci-fi horror Under the Skin, starring Scarlett Johansson, were also filmed at the estate.

"The idea it was described as Scotland's Chernobyl has always been fascinating." said Avezzano, who is working on his first feature - Midgies - a horror film set in Scotland and due to be released next year.

The lead character is played by Jade McDonald who was in the female run of Singin' I'm No a Billy He's a Tim, a play about a Celtic fan and a Rangers fan locked in a prison cell together on the day of an Old Firm match.

Behind has been taken on a tour of international film festivals, including in Italy and Argentina, following its premiere at Glasgow Film Festival's Frightfest.

It was nominated for the best editing prize at Basingstoke's Exit 6 Film Festival and won best international short at Roswell Shorts Festival in New Mexico.

articles.title: Former 'American Idol' star Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for wife's murder amid affair; singer insists 'I did not kill my wife'
articles.summary: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on \"American Idol\" was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole
articles.body: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on "American Idol" was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole Monday after a jury convicted him of murdering his wife while he was having an affair.Caleb Flynn stages wife's murderProsecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, staged a home invasion in February after shooting Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old schoolteacher and volleyball coach, then claimed she was killed by a burglar.In his 2013 appearance on "American Idol," Flynn told TV viewers about how his wife had encouraged him to chase his dreams on the singing competition. He did not advance to the main competition in Hollywood.Caleb Flynn apologises in courtWith tears rolling down his cheeks, Flynn apologized in court to his family, starting with his two daughters."I made vows to Ashley on our wedding day. I failed in those vows," he said.Caleb Flynn claims innocenseAlthough he admitted he lied about many things, Flynn remained adamant that he was innocent."As I stand here before God, who is my ultimate judge, I am not lying when I say I did not kill my wife," he said.Miami County Common Pleas Judge Jeannine Pratt said she was deeply disturbed that Flynn used his faith to hide his "deceit" and "lust."She quoted a victim statement from one of the daughters, read aloud moments earlier by a family member, asking: "What did Ashley ever do to make you hate her so much?"Caleb Flynn's text messages to lover shown in courtDuring closing arguments, prosecutors told jurors that Flynn wanted out of his marriage when he shot his wife at their house in Tipp City, a suburb north of Dayton. The couple's two daughters were home with their father when police arrived.He sent a text message to his lover the night before the shooting, saying, "I choose you. I'm free. Actions will come tomorrow," prosecutors said.During the trial, Alleigha Botner testified she met Flynn in 2022 while she was a 20-year-old intern at his church and had an affair with him for more than a year. She told jurors that Flynn said he hated his wife and had thoughts of killing her.Jurors also heard AI-generated love songs that prosecutors said he made for Botner. Flynn didn't testify on his own behalf, nor did anybody else.Gun used in crime 'not found'The gun used to kill Ashley Flynn was not found at the scene, and his attorney told jurors that investigators found no evidence that Caleb Flynn fired a gun that day. Prosecutors said his fingerprints and DNA were at the scene and that his devices showed him moving around the house, even though he claimed he was asleep at the time of the shooting.The jury found him guilty of murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
